# Project Yaadhum

> Project Yaadhum is a field research initiative studying how students in
> Tier 2 and Tier 3 Tamil Nadu schools arrive at their academic stream and
> pathway decisions after Class 10, and who actually makes those decisions.
> It is based in Cuddalore, Tamil Nadu, India, and began work in 2025.
> The legal entity, Yaadhum Foundation, is in the process of being registered
> as a nonprofit education and research organisation.

Tagline: Every possibility belongs to every student.

The name comes from the Sangam-era Tamil line "Yaadhum oore, yaavarum kelir"
(யாதும் ஊரே யாவரும் கேளிர் — "every town is our own, every person our kin"),
attributed to Kaniyan Pungundranar, Purananuru 192. The organisation treats
that line as a testable premise rather than a slogan: if no accident of birth
decides what belongs to whom, then the district a student is born in should
not quietly decide which academic stream is available to them.

## What the research is about

Of every hundred Tamil Nadu students, roughly 66 enter the science stream and
about 2 choose arts; the remainder go to commerce, vocational routes, or out.
That distribution is documented. How each of those students arrived at their
outcome, whether it was chosen or simply defaulted into, is not. Project
Yaadhum conducts fieldwork in partner schools to record who decides, what
information reaches a family and when, and what it costs when it arrives late.

The method is fieldwork: researchers sit with principals, teachers, students
and parents and write down what is actually happening. It is not a survey
instrument, not a psychometric model, and not a predictive system.

## What Project Yaadhum is not

- It does not sell anything to schools. Pilots are free, with no fee now or later.
- It does not produce career scores, percentages, predictions or rankings of students.
- It does not diagnose students or attach permanent labels to them.
- It is not a coaching centre, a tuition service, or an admissions consultancy.
- It is not an ed-tech platform, an app, or an assessment product.
- It does not track, monitor or profile children.

## Programmes

- Yaadhum Schools: a free pilot inside one class of a partner school. One
  section of roughly 30 to 50 students, about 45 minutes of one period, findings
  shared back to the school. There is no fee, now or later.
- Yaadhum Foundation: free community programmes for students in Classes 9 to 12
  and their parents, run with colleges and local partners, for families who may
  never meet Yaadhum through a school.
- Volunteering: open to college students, B.Ed and teacher-training students and
  recent graduates, 18 or older, anywhere in Tamil Nadu. Training in interviewing,
  facilitation, consent and safeguarding is provided. The work is unpaid.

## People

- Komala Maran, Founder. Studied at IIIT Allahabad, seven years in strategy
  consulting. Mentors students as a volunteer through Naan Mudhalvan
  (TNSkill Corporation) and the Ministry of Education's Vidyanjali programme.
- Abisho George, Founding Member. Mentors students as a volunteer through
  Naan Mudhalvan and the Ministry of Education's Vidyanjali programme.

Those are volunteer mentoring roles held by individuals. The United Nations,
the Ministry of Education and Naan Mudhalvan are not affiliated with Project
Yaadhum and do not endorse, certify or accredit its work.

## Handling of student information

Parent or guardian consent is obtained before any minor takes part. Students are
never scored, ranked, profiled or labelled. A school receives findings about its
own students; a family receives its own child's output; volunteers, sponsors and
the public receive neither. Anything published is anonymised.

across the state.
